description:
## Why

`pkix-lint-cabf` ships CA/B Forum lint bundles as reference / not authoritative interpretations. CA/B Forum publishes only PDFs. zlint (Go, Apache-2.0, Let's Encrypt + community) is the de facto machine-readable interpretation everyone in the CA world cross-checks against. Re-authoring zlint's catalog from scratch is wasted effort and divergence risk.

**Decision (2026-05-11, Mark):** vendor zlint's lint catalog as OSCAL Catalog JSON; the `pkix-lint-cabf` crate interprets the vendored JSON at runtime. No codegen of Rust constants from zlint; consistent with the OSCAL Arch 2 stance ("interpret, don't bind") established in PKIX-ztmr.

## What

### Maintainer-only refresh tool

Add a tool under `pkix-difftest/python/` (or as a Rust binary in a dev-only sub-crate; final shape TBD) that:

1. Runs `zlint -listLintsJSON` against a pinned zlint release tag.
2. Transforms zlint's JSON shape to OSCAL Catalog JSON shape:
   - `zlint.Name` → `control.id`
   - `zlint.Description` → `control.parts[name=statement].prose`
   - `zlint.Citation` (e.g., "BRs: 7.1.4.2.2") → `control.links[rel=cites]` + `control.props[name=br-section]`
   - `zlint.Source` (e.g., "CABFBaselineRequirements") → `control.props[name=source-classification]`
   - `zlint.EffectiveDate` → `control.props[name=effective-date]`
3. Filters by `Source` to emit per-profile catalogs:
   - `cabf-br-tls-derived-from-zlint-v3.X.Y.oscal.json`
   - `cabf-br-smime-derived-from-zlint-v3.X.Y.oscal.json`
   - `cabf-br-cs-derived-from-zlint-v3.X.Y.oscal.json`
4. Writes vendored output to `pkix-lint-cabf/catalogs/`.
5. Refreshed manually when bumping the pinned zlint version. NOT a build-time dep — the refresh produces committable artifacts.

### `pkix-lint-cabf` runtime

1. Bakes the vendored OSCAL Catalog JSON via `include_str!()` (one per profile family).
2. On first use, parses into an in-memory catalog representation. Per OSCAL Arch 2 (PKIX-9vnx.3 onward), parsing yields lean Rust types or `serde_json::Value` walked at lookup time; not 1:1 OSCAL-mirror structs.
3. Rust `Lint` impls reference Control IDs as `&'static str` constants matching the catalog IDs.
4. Startup invariant: each registered Rust `Lint` must have a matching Control in the catalog. Mismatch is a hard error at boot, not silent at runtime.

### What we author by hand

- `check_cert()` body of each Rust `Lint` impl — the actual cert-shape predicate using `x509-cert` / `der`.
- `divergences.md` documenting where pkix-lint-cabf's interpretation intentionally differs from zlint's, with rationale.

### What we DO NOT author

- Lint metadata (title, description, citation, effective date, source classification).
- Lint catalog organization (what lints exist, how they're grouped by Source).
- Test fixture corpus organization (option to vendor zlint's `testdata/` per-lint cert fixtures separately — filed under PKIX-hbzo.1 cross-validation oracle work).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Refresh tool exists under `pkix-difftest/python/` (or sub-crate; chosen at implementation time).
- [ ] zlint version pinned in tool source + in refreshed catalog filenames.
- [ ] At least one vendored OSCAL Catalog (start with `cabf-br-tls`) checked into `pkix-lint-cabf/catalogs/`.
- [ ] Catalog validates against NIST OSCAL Catalog v1.2.2 schema (per PKIX-9vnx.1 pinning).
- [ ] `pkix-lint-cabf` runtime parses + indexes the catalog; startup-invariant check on registered Lint IDs.
- [ ] At least one Rust `Lint` impl referencing a catalog Control ID, demonstrating the pairing pattern.
- [ ] Attribution: header comment in each vendored catalog crediting zlint + version + URL + Apache-2.0 notice.
- [ ] `divergences.md` placeholder file exists in `pkix-lint-cabf/`, ready to grow as divergences accumulate.

## Out of scope

- Implementing all 100+ CA/B Forum lints in this bead. This bead establishes the pattern with 1+ example; the rest grow incrementally.
- pkilint-derived catalog (pkilint has different lint organization; cross-validation only per PKIX-hbzo.1).
- Generating an OSCAL Catalog for the RFC-conformance lints in `pkix-lint`. Those are workspace-authored, not zlint-derived.

## Depends on

- `PKIX-amgn.3` (pkix-lint-cabf crate exists — CLOSED 2026-05-11, stub shipped).
- `PKIX-9vnx.6` (Lint trait has metadata methods that can be matched against Control IDs).

## Relationship to other beads

- **Reshapes PKIX-amgn.5.** The substantive `pkix-lint-cabf` content (originally framed as "author lint bundles by hand from PDF reading") becomes "implement Rust `check_cert()` bodies referencing zlint-derived Catalog IDs."
- **Pairs with PKIX-hbzo.1** (cross-validation oracle). zlint as the catalog-of-record + zlint as a runtime oracle is mutually reinforcing.
- **Anchored by PKIX-8qz1** (per-rule split). zlint catalogs are policy interpretations of CA/B Forum BR; they live in `-cabf` reference crates. Rust does the executable side.

## Filed by

Surfaced in conversation 2026-05-11 after reasoning through "CA/B Forum publishes only PDFs; zlint is the de facto machine-readable form; could we treat it as the data source?" Mark chose interpret-at-runtime over codegen, consistent with Arch 2 OSCAL stance.
notes: Re-scoped 2026-05-12 (PKIX-ncab.2, decision B): OSCAL demoted as canonical format. The zlint catalog vendoring goal is still valid — pkix-lint-cabf wants to track zlint's living rule set rather than re-encode by hand — but the OSCAL Catalog JSON target is no longer prescribed. Output format is TBD pending the (not-yet-filed) replacement policy/config format decision. Closed children .8.1 + .8.2 remain as decision-history. Open children .8.3-.8.6 are snapshots of the OSCAL-target version of this work and have been labeled human; they will be reworked, closed, or replaced when the format decision lands. See memory pkix-oscal-demoted-2026-05-11.
